post_text:
I trusted green dashboards over actual thread health.

Squeezing every microsecond out of our JVM stack was my specialty, so I aggressively tuned our HikariCP connection pool parameters to eliminate lifecycle churn.

I set the maximum connection lifetime to four hours, extending far past standard safety guidelines. Database throughput jumped immediately, allocation overhead dropped to zero, and our monitoring dashboards glowed a reassuring, uninterrupted green.

We celebrated what looked like a textbook performance optimization.

A nagging feeling crept in as asynchronous background tasks quietly accumulated retries without triggering p99 latency alarms.

Deep within the infra layer, a stateful firewall was silently dropping idle TCP connections after twenty minutes of inactivity.

HikariCP kept handing out these dead handles, causing threads to block indefinitely until the entire thread pool starved to death.

What I learned:

Green metrics mask deep structural failures when transient infrastructure silently invalidates your application state.
